item.title: Two Runners Die After Collapsing in Siksorogo Lawu Ultra During Harsh Weather
item.description: Karanganyar, Central Java. Two participants in the Siksorogo Lawu Ultra 2025 died during the 15-kilometer Fun Run segment on Sunday after collapsing on steep mountain trails amid heavy rain. Karanganyar Police confirmed that the first report reached authorities at 11:30 a.m., shortly after fellow runners discovered a participant unconscious on the Mitis Hill trail at kilometer 12. item.title: Businesses Expect 5.0-5.4% GDP Growth in 2026, No Big Blow from Sumatra Floods
item.description: Jakarta. The Indonesian Employers Association, or Apindo, projects the national economy to expand between 5.0 percent and 5.4 percent year-on-year (yoy) in 2026, as the group doubts the Sumatra floods will take a dramatic toll on the national gross domestic product (GDP). According to Apindo’s estimates, the Q1 festivities will be a major GDP growth driver in 2026. item.title: Purbaya Flags 2026 Export Duty to Boost State Revenue
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia is advancing a new gold export duty as part of efforts to secure domestic supply, expand the bullion-bank ecosystem, and accelerate value-added processing at home, a move that comes amid soaring global prices and declining ore reserves. Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa said on Monday that Indonesia, despite being the world’s fourth-largest holder of gold reserves, available ore has been trending lower while domestic demand continues to rise. item.title: Northern Japan Hit by Powerful 7.5 Quake; Tsunami Waves Strike Coast
item.description: Tokyo. A powerful magnitude 7.5 earthquake struck off northern Japan late Monday, injuring 23 people and triggering a small tsunami along the Pacific coast, officials said. Authorities warned of possible aftershocks and an increased risk of a larger quake. The government was still assessing the damage from the late-evening temblor and tsunami. item.title: No Indonesian Victim in Japan’s 7.5-Magnitude Quake
item.description: Jakarta. The government confirmed Tuesday that the recent powerful 7.5 magnitude quake that rocked Japan did not claim any Indonesian victims. The powerful quake struck the eastern coast of Aomori prefecture on Monday at around 11.15 p.m. local time. Japan is home to hundreds of thousands of Indonesian citizens, some of whom are students. item.description: Jakarta. Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) opened at 8,743 on Tuesday, climbing 33 points or 0.38 percent in early trade and once again setting a fresh all-time high. item.title: Palm Oil Extends Slide as Stronger Ringgit, Rising Stocks Pressure Prices
item.description: Jakarta. Palm oil prices continued to weaken on Monday, with the benchmark contract falling to 4,064 ringgit ($986.65) per tonne on Tuesday, down 0.73 percent from the previous day, according to CFD market data. Prices have slipped 1.14 percent over the past month and are now 17.98 percent lower than a year earlier. item.title: ‘Indonesia Must Not End Up Trapped Like Malaysia’: Businesses on US Tariff Talks
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesian businesses are keeping their fingers crossed that Jakarta will not fall into the same trap as Malaysia did in its US tariff negotiations.
